## setting
**100 run(s)** — rule `yu26-setting` — 10.1111/pce.70649  
*Methods and Materials, 'Sorghum Growth and Field Experiment Setup'; Results*

> All plants were well-watered (WW) at the same rate (~24%, SVWC, corresponding approximately to the soil field capacity) until flag leaf appearance in the whorl (~47 days after planting). After this point in time, two replicates of the six genotypes were maintained at WW conditions for the remainder of the season, while three replicates were subjected to water deficit stress (water-limited [WL]) to mimic drought; this corresponded to an SVWC of 16%. | Results: 'plants were grown in replicated plots as part of a large field trial. All plants were irrigated at normal rates (control conditions) until the reproductive stage (appearance of the flag leaf), after which a drought treatment was implemented by reducing irrigation to a subset of plots'. Soil water was monitored by neutron probe at four depths with an AZMET weather station on site; a whole growing season to harvest on 4 November 2020.
